title: General Data Protection Regulation — Regulation (EU) 2016/679
summary: The EU's general data-protection law, published in the OJ on 4 May 2016 and applicable from 25 May 2018; Arts. 5, 6, 9, 22 and 35 are the main GDPR hooks used against AI training, profiling and automated decision-making.

title: Digital Services Act — Regulation (EU) 2022/2065
summary: Sets due-diligence, content-moderation and systemic-risk duties for online intermediaries and very large online platforms; published in the OJ on 27 October 2022, applicable from 17 February 2024. It is the legal basis for the Commission's DSA proceedings against X/Grok.

title: European AI Office established — Commission Decision C/2024/1459
summary: Establishes the European AI Office within DG CNECT to implement and enforce the AI Act, especially the rules for general-purpose AI models. Decision of 24 January 2024, published in the OJ on 14 February 2024, in force 21 February 2024.
notes: Decision of 24 January 2024, published in the OJ on 14 February 2024.

title: EU AI Act — Regulation (EU) 2024/1689
summary: The world's first comprehensive AI law: risk-based rules for AI systems, prohibitions, high-risk obligations, GPAI duties and transparency duties. Adopted 13 June 2024, published in the OJ on 12 July 2024, in force 1 August 2024.
next_milestone: 2 Dec 2027: high-risk duties begin (Annex III stand-alone systems)

title: EDPB Opinion 28/2024 on AI models and personal data
summary: EDPB opinion (requested by the Irish DPC) on when an AI model trained on personal data can be considered anonymous, when legitimate interest is a lawful basis for training/deployment, and the consequences of unlawful training data.

title: Commission Guidelines on prohibited AI practices (Art. 5 AI Act)
summary: Non-binding Commission guidelines interpreting the eight prohibited AI practices (manipulation, exploitation of vulnerabilities, social scoring, crime-risk prediction, untargeted facial scraping, emotion recognition, biometric categorisation, real-time remote biometric identification). The prohibitions applied from 2 February 2025.
source_title: European Commission, Guidelines on prohibited AI practices (C(2025) 884 final, published 4 Feb 2025; formally adopted as C(2025) 5052 final, 29 Jul 2025)
notes: The prohibitions applied from 2 February 2025. Content approved 4 Feb 2025 as C(2025) 884 final; formally adopted 29 Jul 2025 as C(2025) 5052 final.

title: General-Purpose AI Code of Practice
summary: Voluntary code drawn up by 13 independent experts with ~1,000 stakeholders, in three chapters (Transparency, Copyright, Safety and Security), to help GPAI providers demonstrate compliance with Arts. 53 and 55 AI Act. Confirmed by the Commission and AI Board as an adequate voluntary compliance tool.
notes: Drawn up by 13 independent experts with ~1,000 stakeholders; three chapters (Transparency, Copyright, Safety and Security).

title: Digital Omnibus on AI — Regulation (EU) 2026/1744
summary: Amends the AI Act to simplify implementation: postpones high-risk application dates (2 Dec 2027 for stand-alone Annex III systems; 2 Aug 2028 for Annex I product-embedded systems), narrows some duties, and adds two new prohibited practices (Art. 5(1)(ba)–(bb)): AI systems generating non-consensual intimate material and child sexual abuse material, applicable from 2 Dec 2026. Published in the OJ 24 July 2026, in force 27 July 2026.
next_milestone: 2 Dec 2026: new Art. 5 prohibitions (ba)–(bb) apply; 2 Dec 2027: high-risk duties begin (Annex III stand-alone systems); 2 Aug 2028: Annex I product-embedded systems

title: France — National Strategy for Artificial Intelligence
summary: Launched March 2018 following the Villani report; €1,527m public funding for 2018–2022 across research, higher education, public transformation, economy and defence/security, with an acceleration phase announced November 2021 for 2022–2025.
source_title: Ministère de l'Économie, Stratégie nationale pour l'IA, 2e phase — dossier de presse, 8 Nov 2021
notes: Following the Villani report; €1,527m public funding for 2018–2022; acceleration phase announced November 2021 for 2022–2025.

title: Germany — AI Strategy of the Federal Government
summary: Federal strategy adopted 15 November 2018 and updated 2 December 2020, aiming for competitive, human-centric and trustworthy "AI made in Germany"; initial €3bn to 2025, raised to ~€5bn in the 2020 update, which added pandemic, sustainability and health priorities.
source_title: Die Bundesregierung, Strategie Künstliche Intelligenz — Fortschreibung 2020 (Dec 2020)
notes: Updated 2 December 2020; initial €3bn to 2025, raised to ~€5bn in the 2020 update.

title: Denmark — National Strategy for Artificial Intelligence
summary: Government strategy (Ministry of Finance and Ministry of Industry, Business and Financial Affairs), March 2019, aiming to make Denmark a front-runner in responsible AI use, with four objectives (ethical human-centric basis, research, business growth, world-class public services) and 24 initiatives.

title: Netherlands — Strategic Action Plan for Artificial Intelligence (SAPAI)
summary: Government of the Netherlands action plan built on three pillars: capitalising on societal/economic opportunities, creating the right conditions (education, research, data, connectivity), and strengthening foundations (public values, human rights, trust and safety).
source_title: Tweede Kamer, Parliamentary Papers blg-903667 (SAPAI report)

title: Poland — Policy for the Development of Artificial Intelligence in Poland from 2020
summary: Council of Ministers Resolution No. 196 of 28 December 2020 (Monitor Polski 2021, item 23) setting short-, medium- and long-term AI goals across six areas: society, innovative companies, science, education, international cooperation and the public sector.
notes: Council of Ministers Resolution No. 196 of 28 December 2020.

title: Ireland — National AI Strategy, "AI – Here for Good"
summary: Ireland's first national AI strategy, launched 8 July 2021 by the Taoiseach and the Department of Enterprise, Trade and Employment; a whole-of-government roadmap for trustworthy, human-centric AI adoption in enterprise and public services, refreshed in November 2024.

title: Spain — AESIA created, Royal Decree 729/2023
summary: Royal Decree 729/2023 of 22 August 2023 approves the statute of the Agencia Española de Supervisión de la Inteligencia Artificial (AESIA), based in A Coruña — the first EU member-state AI supervision agency, later Spain's AI market-surveillance authority and single point of contact. Published in the BOE on 2 September 2023.
notes: Published in the BOE on 2 September 2023; based in A Coruña; Spain's AI market-surveillance authority and single point of contact.

title: Spain — Artificial Intelligence Strategy 2024
summary: Council of Ministers approval on 14 May 2024 of the updated AI strategy (continuing the 2020 ENIA), structured in three axes and eight levers — supercomputing, Spanish/co-official-language models (ALIA), public- and private-sector uptake, and transparent, ethical, humanistic AI — with €1.5bn for 2024–2025.

title: Italy — AI Law, Legge 23 settembre 2025, n. 132
summary: Italy's comprehensive national AI law ("Disposizioni e deleghe al Governo in materia di intelligenza artificiale"), the first such law in the EU; it sets a biennial national AI strategy, designates AgID and the National Cybersecurity Agency (ACN) as national AI authorities, and adds AI-related criminal offences. Published in Gazzetta Ufficiale No. 223 on 25 September 2025, in force 10 October 2025.
notes: First comprehensive national AI law in the EU; in force 10 October 2025.
